investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (resource quota exhausted or peer-pod slots fully consumed), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable on both resource-constrained nodes. Because the pod remained unscheduled for ~141–145 seconds across all three checks, the agent VM was never created, and the eval runner received no evidence to validate against the expected-output contract (vmIdPresent=true, remoteState in [running, idle, ready]).

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: the extended resource quota for peer-pod VMs is fully consumed, leaving no capacity for new pods. This is the direct message from the scheduler across all three checks.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector, which may indicate a label was removed, a node was replaced without the required label, or the pod spec targets a node group that no longer exists at sufficient scale.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total number of nodes carrying kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity (2) may be insufficient for concurrent eval runs or concurrent production workloads, causing resource contention.

Lower probability — a recent change to the pod spec (node affinity rules or resource requests) that reduced the schedulable node set; however, sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges is empty and no pod-spec change is present in the supplied evidence, so this remains speculative.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted by the eval runner was left unschedulable: the two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence payloads were collected by any check, so the contract-required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) are entirely absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure failure scoped to the remote-agent Kubernetes scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place any remote-agent pod on the 6-node cluster at the time of the eval run (2026-07-08T16:52–16:57Z). The scheduler message is consistent across all three sibling checks: "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector." Because no pod was ever scheduled, the agent was never created, and the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) never returned an agent identity. Consequently the probe could not poll state, and zero evidence fields were written — causing the contract validation to fail on all four required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state). The root cause is exhaustion of the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the two eligible nodes, combined with the remaining four nodes being ineligible due to node affinity or selector mismatch.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' — pod was unscheduled for 143s before the check timed out.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four contract fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) are missing, consistent with the probe aborting before createAgent returned.
sibling.remote-agent-create: identical scheduler message, latencyMs=148704, empty evidenceKeys — the upstream create check failed for the same reason before remote-agent-state even started.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler message, latencyMs=151002, empty evidenceKeys — the downstream runtime check also failed, confirming the scheduling block persisted across the full eval window (~5 minutes).

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:258-266: contract at line 264 requires [orgId, agentId, readyState, state] — none were produced.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on both eligible nodes — concurrent workloads or a prior eval run that did not clean up VMs may have exhausted the pool, leaving no capacity for new pods.

[Likely contributing] Node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod restricts scheduling to only the two kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes, so the four remaining nodes cannot serve as fallback even when the vm resource is unavailable.
[Possible] A VM or peer-pod that was created by a previous eval run was not released (cleanup failure in withCleanup), holding the kata.peerpods.io/vm slot and preventing new allocations.

[Possible] The kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the two eligible nodes was reduced (e.g., node reconfiguration, node replacement, or resource limit change) without a corresponding change to the cluster capacity available to the eval workload.
[Lower confidence] A transient spike in legitimate remote-agent usage by other workloads temporarily exhausted the vm resource pool at the time of the eval run.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (resource quota exhausted or peer-pod slots fully consumed), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable on both resource-constrained nodes. Because the pod remained unscheduled for ~141–145 seconds across all three checks, the agent VM was never created, and the eval runner received no evidence to validate against the expected-output contract (vmIdPresent=true, remoteState in [running, idle, ready]).

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message for 145s, same node breakdown

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 4 required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=148704, check timed out well before the outageLatencyMs threshold of 360000ms, confirming the failure was a hard scheduling block rather than a slow boot

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready], neither of which can be satisfied without a running VM
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: the extended resource quota for peer-pod VMs is fully consumed, leaving no capacity for new pods. This is the direct message from the scheduler across all three checks.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector, which may indicate a label was removed, a node was replaced without the required label, or the pod spec targets a node group that no longer exists at sufficient scale.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total number of nodes carrying kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity (2) may be insufficient for concurrent eval runs or concurrent production workloads, causing resource contention.

Lower probability — a recent change to the pod spec (node affinity rules or resource requests) that reduced the schedulable node set; however, sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges is empty and no pod-spec change is present in the supplied evidence, so this remains speculative.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted by the eval runner was left unschedulable: the two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence payloads were collected by any check, so the contract-required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) are entirely absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure failure scoped to the remote-agent Kubernetes scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place any remote-agent pod on the 6-node cluster at the time of the eval run (2026-07-08T16:52–16:57Z). The scheduler message is consistent across all three sibling checks: "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector." Because no pod was ever scheduled, the agent was never created, and the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) never returned an agent identity. Consequently the probe could not poll state, and zero evidence fields were written — causing the contract validation to fail on all four required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state). The root cause is exhaustion of the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the two eligible nodes, combined with the remaining four nodes being ineligible due to node affinity or selector mismatch.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' — pod was unscheduled for 143s before the check timed out.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=147374, status=fail, endedAt=2026-07-08T16:55:05.671Z — the check ran to near its warningLatencyMs threshold (240000ms) before failing.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no fields were written, confirming the runner never reached the agent-creation or state-polling steps.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four contract fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) are missing, consistent with the probe aborting before createAgent returned.
sibling.remote-agent-create: identical scheduler message, latencyMs=148704, empty evidenceKeys — the upstream create check failed for the same reason before remote-agent-state even started.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler message, latencyMs=151002, empty evidenceKeys — the downstream runtime check also failed, confirming the scheduling block persisted across the full eval window (~5 minutes).

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1897-1905: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1905 immediately after acquiring orgId — if the pod is never scheduled, this call will block or error and no evidence is written.
source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:258-266: contract at line 264 requires [orgId, agentId, readyState, state] — none were produced.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on both eligible nodes — concurrent workloads or a prior eval run that did not clean up VMs may have exhausted the pool, leaving no capacity for new pods.

[Likely contributing] Node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod restricts scheduling to only the two kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes, so the four remaining nodes cannot serve as fallback even when the vm resource is unavailable.
[Possible] A VM or peer-pod that was created by a previous eval run was not released (cleanup failure in withCleanup), holding the kata.peerpods.io/vm slot and preventing new allocations.

[Possible] The kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the two eligible nodes was reduced (e.g., node reconfiguration, node replacement, or resource limit change) without a corresponding change to the cluster capacity available to the eval workload.
[Lower confidence] A transient spike in legitimate remote-agent usage by other workloads temporarily exhausted the vm resource pool at the time of the eval run.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes swarm cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector, leaving 0 of 6 nodes available for scheduling. Because no agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the point of creating an agent or receiving a runtime response, so all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent and the expected-output contract is entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing remote agent provisioning has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector requirements. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. With no schedulable node available and preemption unable to free capacity (no preemption victims found), every remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure that prevents the eval runner from ever calling createAgent, making all downstream evidence collection and contract assertions impossible. This is an eval-observed infrastructure failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota is fully consumed on the 2 affinity-matching nodes, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. No preemption victims exist, so the scheduler cannot free slots automatically.

Secondary: The 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector requirements (e.g., a label or taint mismatch), reducing the effective scheduling domain to only 2 nodes, both of which are at capacity.

Tertiary: A prior eval run or external workload may have left orphaned remote-agent pods running on the 2 affinity-matching nodes, consuming all available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without releasing them.

Lower confidence: A cluster scaling event, node drain, or node failure may have reduced the number of affinity-matching nodes from a larger pool to only 2, shrinking available capacity below the demand threshold.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately inspect the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes for running or stuck remote-agent pods that may be holding all available VM slots; terminate any orphaned pods to free capacity.

Check whether the remote-agents eval cleanup path (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs line 1916) is reliably releasing pods after each run; if cleanup is failing, leaked pods will exhaust capacity across successive runs.

Verify node affinity/selector configuration for remote-agent pods against the labels present on all 6 cluster nodes to determine whether the scheduling domain is unintentionally restricted to only 2 nodes.

If the 2 affinity-matching nodes are genuinely at capacity, evaluate whether additional kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes can be added to the cluster or whether the per-node VM limit can be increased.
After restoring capacity, re-run all three remote-agents checks to confirm recovery before closing the investigation.

Review the feature registry configuration (features.json lines 187-188): degradedAfterFailures=1 and outageAfterFailures=2 mean this feature will be marked degraded after a single failure; ensure alerting thresholds are appropriate for transient scheduling pressure.

recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Determines whether orphaned or long-running remote-agent pods from prior eval runs are consuming the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, which would explain why no capacity is available for new pods.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If a subsequent eval run succeeds and returns all 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) without any cluster changes, the scheduling exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a transient scheduler glitch would be more likely.

If kubectl describe on the pending pods shows a different failure reason (e.g., image pull error, resource quota at namespace level, or admission webhook rejection) rather than kata.peerpods.io/vm insufficiency, the root cause would need to be revised.

If the 4 non-affinity-matching nodes are found to actually satisfy the pod's affinity/selector after label inspection, the node affinity mismatch sub-cause would be disproved and the failure would be solely attributable to the 2-node capacity exhaustion.

If no remote-agent pods are currently running on the 2 affinity-matching nodes (i.e., kata.peerpods.io/vm slots are free), the exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and a misconfigured resource limit or quota would become the primary suspect.

If only remote-agent-runtime fails while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state pass in a subsequent run, the shared scheduling failure hypothesis would be disproved and the issue would be localized to the runtime check specifically.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that probes kata.peerpods.io/vm resource availability on affinity-matching nodes before attempting agent creation, surfacing capacity exhaustion as a distinct check rather than a timeout.

Add a pod-scheduling health check that verifies at least one node is schedulable for remote-agent pods (correct affinity labels and available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots) as a prerequisite gate before running remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime.
Add a cleanup-verification eval that confirms no orphaned remote-agent pods remain after each eval run, catching resource leaks before they exhaust cluster capacity.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that asserts the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector is above a minimum threshold (e.g., at least 3), alerting when the scheduling domain shrinks unexpectedly.
